Deceptive patterns & habitual behaviour in web shops
Deceptive patterns and habitual behaviour in web shops

Deceptive patterns are mostly studied as visual design, but much of the manipulation works through habit: you click where you've clicked yesterday. Little empirical research exists on that cognitive mechanism.
Deceptive patterns en gewoontegedrag in webshops

Deceptive patterns worden vooral bestudeerd als visueel ontwerp, maar veel manipulatie werkt via gewoontes: je klikt waar je gisteren ook klikte. Over dat cognitieve mechanisme bestaat nog weinig empirisch onderzoek.

I'm Robert Karzijn. My interest lies at the intersection of people and technology: how people use interfaces, which habits form along the way, and how design (deliberately or not) plays into that. In my bachelor's thesis I experimentally investigated how web shops can disrupt procedural memory by relocating interface elements.

I'm currently pursuing a master's in Human-Computer Interaction, focusing on cognitive UX and ethical interface design. Outside study and work: photography, audio and the occasional evening of gaming.

In mijn bachelorthesis onderzocht ik experimenteel hoe webshops procedureel geheugen kunnen verstoren door interface elementen te verplaatsen.

MobiPad trailer thumbnail: "Your iPhone is a game controller. For emulators on your Mac", next to an iPhone showing the controller layout
